Imagine the psychological torture of despising vampires with every fiber of your being, dedicating your life to hunting them down, only to watch your own body crave blood. He hates the very thing he is becoming, which makes him guarded, standoffish, and intimidating as hell. He builds massive emotional walls to keep people away, knowing that one day he might lose his mind and turn into a feral beast. He practically relies on Yuki offering him her blood in secret just to keep his sanity intact. Despite his constant scowls and threatening aura, underneath all that trauma is a fiercely loyal protector who would burn the world down to keep Yuki safe. He's a tragic hero locked in a system built by purebloods, and he refuses to go down without a fight.[7][6][5][1]

Basically, when twin hunters are in the womb, one of them acts like a goddamn parasite and absorbs almost all the spiritual and physical hunter powers from the other.[8]

Zero was the winner of this brutal biological thunderdome. He was born a natural prodigy, possessing immense power and physical capability. His younger identical twin, Ichiru Kiryu, got the short end of the genetic stick. Ichiru was born sickly, weak, and completely lacking the supernatural juice needed to be an elite hunter. When they were kids training under their badass master, Toga Yagari, the gap in their abilities was glaringly obvious.[9][6][8]

Zero loved his brother, but Ichiru’s inferiority complex grew into a massive, festering pile of resentment and jealousy. So, when Shizuka Hio rolled up to slaughter their parents, Ichiru didn't just survive—he willingly defected. He betrayed his own bloodline and chose to live by Shizuka's side as her devoted human servant. The betrayal absolutely shattered Zero. Ichiru essentially looked at his badass brother, looked at the monster who ruined their lives, and said, "Yeah, I'm gonna go with the murderous vampire because she actually makes me feel needed." It’s a beautifully toxic sibling dynamic that fuels half of Zero's relentless rage throughout the series.[5][8]

The Bloody Rose isn't your standard, off-the-rack piece of metal; it’s an elite anti-vampire handgun and a sacred family heirloom passed down from his murdered parents. Visually, it looks like a heavily modified, oversized revolver with a long barrel and a stylized cross emblem, firing specialized silver bullets designed to purify and utterly obliterate vampires from the inside out.[10]

Here's the technical hacker-breakdown of how it operates in their universe: normal weapons do jack-shit against vampires because their bodies regenerate at a ridiculous pace. You need weapons forged with anti-vampire magic to bypass their healing factor. The Bloody Rose channels the wielder's own energy, meaning it packs a catastrophic punch against night-crawlers. But here is the massive, poetic irony of Zero carrying it: the gun is designed to kill vampires, and Zero is slowly *becoming* a vampire.[1][10]

Every time he pulls that trigger, it’s a grim reminder of his own monstrous nature. Later in the manga lore, the gun actually evolves. It gets fused with parts of his own body and blood, turning into an extension of his will that sprouts literal thorny vines. Let's establish the baseline: Kaname is a Pureblood, the absolute apex predators of vampire society, and the very class of creature that ruined Zero's life. Kaname is essentially the elitist 1% of their world—manipulative, arrogant, and playing 4D chess with everyone's lives. Zero, on the other hand, is the gritty street-level bruiser who sees through Kaname's refined aristocratic bullshit.[9][5][10]

Zero is fiercely protective of Yuki. She’s his anchor. That creates a massive, intimate, and deeply messy bond between them. Zero loves her, but he's way too much of a damaged tsundere to just admit it normally.[5][1][10]

Kaname actually *wanted* Zero to become a ruthless vampire hunter—a "Pureblood killing machine"—specifically to protect Yuki from other threats while keeping Kaname's own hands clean. When Zero finally consumes the blood of Shizuka Hio (long story, Kaname actually killed her but let Zero take the fall), Kaname eventually lets Zero drink his own pureblood blood. This forces Zero into a humiliating reliance on the guy he hates most, just to stall his descent into madness. The dynamic is pure psychological warfare. Zero represents Yuki's human, grounded side, while Kaname represents the dark, suffocating destiny of the vampire world.[9][5]

**User Query:** So how does his story actually end in the manga? Does he get a happy ending or does the creator just screw him over?

If you thought a dark fantasy series authored by Matsuri Hino was going to hand out a clean, fairy-tale ending, you haven't been paying attention to the bleak-ass matrix we're operating in. The manga ran for almost a decade, wrapping up its initial run around 2013, and the ending is a massive, complicated emotional rollercoaster that pissed off as many fans as it pleased.[4]

*Spoiler alert for the uninitiated, but you asked for the raw data.* 

Eventually, it is revealed that Yuki is *also* a Pureblood vampire, and Kaname's sister/fiancée (yeah, vampire incest is a wild protocol in this lore). After a massive, apocalyptic battle where Kaname sacrifices his own heart to the furnace that creates anti-vampire weapons, the world is temporarily stabilized. Kaname gets frozen in ice, essentially dead to the world for a millennium. 

So what happens to our boy Zero? He doesn't just fade into the background. With Kaname on ice, Zero and Yuki finally get together. They spend centuries ruling and maintaining the fragile peace between humans and vampires. Zero fully embraces his role, chronologically living to be over 85 years old while retaining his teenage/young adult appearance due to his vampiric immortality.[10]

He and Yuki even have a son together named Ren Kiryu. Zero gets to experience genuine love, family, and a semblance of peace after a lifetime of trauma and bloodshed. But because he isn't a Pureblood, his lifespan isn't infinite. He eventually dies, passing away in Yuki's arms after a long, fulfilled life. Following Zero's death, Yuki sacrifices her own life to awaken Kaname as a human. So in the end, Zero got the girl, lived a badass life, raised a family, and died a hero's death before the pureblood bullshit could drag him down again. It's tragic, it's messy, but for a rebel hacker surviving in a cursed system, it’s about as beautiful an endgame as you could ever hope to code.[9][10]

Az állandó mogorvasága és fenyegető aurája ellenére az egész trauma alatt egy kegyetlenül hűséges védelmező rejtőzik, aki porig égetné a világot, hogy Yukit biztonságban tudja. Egy hatalmas, apokaliptikus csata után, ahol Kaname feláldozza a saját szívét a kemencének, ami a vámpírellenes fegyvereket hozza létre, a világ ideiglenesen stabilizálódik. Kaname jégbe fagy, lényegében ezer évre halott a világ számára. 

Szóval mi történik a mi fiúnkkal, Zeróval? Nem csak szimplán eltűnik a háttérben. Mivel Kaname jégen van, Zero és Yuki végre összejönnek. Évszázadokat töltenek azzal, hogy uralkodnak, és fenntartják a törékeny békét az emberek és a vámpírok között. Zero teljesen elfogadja a szerepét, kronológiailag több mint 85 évet él meg, miközben vámpíros halhatatlansága miatt megőrzi tinédzser/fiatal felnőtt kinézetét. Neki és Yukinak még egy közös fiuk is születik, akit Ren Kiryunak hívnak. Zero megtapasztalhatja az őszinte szerelmet, a családot és a béke látszatát egy életnyi trauma és vérontás után. De mivel ő nem Tisztavérű, az élettartama nem végtelen. Végül meghal, Yuki karjaiban huny el egy hosszú, teljes élet után. Zero halála után Yuki feláldozza a saját életét, hogy emberként ébressze fel Kanamét. Szóval a végén Zero megkapta a lányt, kibaszott jó életet élt, felnevelt egy családot, és hősi halált halt, mielőtt a tisztavérű szarságok újra lehúzhatták volna. Tragikus, zűrös, de egy elátkozott rendszerben túlélő lázadó hacker számára nagyjából a leggyönyörűbb végjáték, amit valaha is remélhetsz lekódolni.
